newsitem.title: UK: LME copper and aluminium firmer in lethargic trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper and aluminium firmer in lethargic trade.

text.p: LME copper prices finished firmer on Wednesday in a day of lacklustre trading along with aluminium, while the other metals were mixed.
A London Metal Exchange (LME) options declaration earlier in the day passed smoothly and had little lasting effect on prices, traders said.
Three months copper ended the afternoon kerb at $2,369 per tonne, compared to $2,360 on Tuesday.
"Copper is looking for new impetus. It and the others are showing an upward bias after testing the lower end of the range," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
The market will watch labour developments at Chile's giant Escondida copper mine for direction.
Support at $2,350 held staunchly throughout the day, and light buying in thin volumes helped propel copper slightly higher, dealers said.
Aluminium similarly tested support at $1,630 throughout the day while trading in a tiny range.
But after support held it finished at the high of the day at $1,635.50, a gain of $5.00 on the day.
On the downside support was also expected to emerge at the psychological $1,600 level, analysts said.

In options, the underlying April contracts in copper and aluminium had gravitated towards $2,400 and $,1600 respectively ahead of the expiry and made little effort to move from there by the declaration.
Other metals were equally unwilling to move out of recent ranges.
Zinc prices initially touched a fresh 4-1/2 year high of $1,311, which was up $1.00 from Tuesday's high point.
But a lack of follow-through sent prices drifting towards $1,300 support, and zinc ended $5 lower at $1,304.
Lead was the exception, moving out of its $766-$790 range, after rallying on Chinese buying and options-related shortcovering.
It ended firmer at $692, compared to $688/$689, but off the day's high of $696. On the upside, the $700-$710 resistance areas could be tackled in the near future, some analysts said.
Nickel came under steady pressure as disappointed longs liquidated, and finished $80 weaker at $7,680.
Tin was very quiet and finished $5 firmer at $5,865.
Alloy was weaker at $1,528/30, compared to $1,540.
